NORTH_PLAN N3 planned a viewer-only web_theater crate to keep the wasm
cfg surface small. Measured, the surface was three mechanical walls:
getrandom needs its browser-entropy features (0.2 takes a cargo
feature; 0.3 additionally reads getrandom_backend from
.cargo/config.toml — both generations live in the graph),
tracing-appender cannot build where symlinks don't exist (moved to the
non-wasm dep table; wasm-release logging installs the filter over a
discarding writer), and the blocking ureq ice fetch has no browser
analogue (cfg'd out; the wasm build runs the STUN-only path, a
gloo-fetch port is the follow-up if browser duels need the relay).

So the web build is the app itself — netplay included, since matchbox
has been browser-native all along — and COMPLETION_PLAN P.5 completes
in full rather than viewer-first. cargo check -p app --target
wasm32-unknown-unknown is clean; the native gate is untouched (552
tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt). Web entry glue, the share loop, the
wasm CI checksum lane, and hosting land next.

noodles/2895223:
The builder heard it before the code showed it: a four-bar drum clip in
the session grid only ever played bar one. clipLengthBars returned 1 for
every non-harmony track, advanceSceneTrack wrapped each clip's step at
that, and the lane index was step-modulo-length - so the editor paged
four bars, the arrangement played four bars (it indexes by absolute bar),
and the session transport never reached step 16. Measured before the fix
(.tmp/pa-phrase-probe.mjs, 9 s of session play at 180): a 64-step drum
lane with hits in all four bars sounded step 0 only, and a 32-step
walking bass never played its second note. The same wrap reset 12-step
polymeter lanes at every barline - a 12+4 stutter where the ? page
promises phasing.

Lane position now runs on st.total, the free-running counter motion
lanes already used, so a lane of any length walks fully and a short lane
phases truly; st.step keeps the clip lifecycle (follow-actions, oneshot,
queue landings). clipLengthBars counts real bars for every track, and
counts harmony in bars rather than entries - a rate-2 scene's eight
half-bar slots are four bars, so its session pie stops filling at half
speed and a queued launch stops waiting out a phantom eight-bar phrase.

Same pass, the cohesion the phrase makes possible: when a lane spans the
scene's whole progression, the editor's BAR chips wear each bar's roman
in its function tint - 1/I 2/vi 3/IV 4/V - so bar three of the beat
knows it lands on the IV without leaving the sheet. A lane shorter than
the phrase cycles against the changes, so its chips stay plain numbers
rather than claim an alignment that rotates.

Verified: phrase probe post-fix reads hits at steps 0/18/36/54 and both
bass notes; polymeter probe reads a true 9-hit 12-cycle across 6.75 bars
(bar-locked was ~13); smoke green; calibrate untouched by construction
(its fixture is 16-step lanes, where total and step coincide).

Holding the door knob still for 400ms opens the home wedge's bloom - the
knob sits on the home wedge and buried its bloom, worst with an
inner-ring home where the zone ate most of the wedge. Still means still:
9px of travel or a candidate wedge cancels the hold, so a slow door drag

The smoke's recurring 'strum wrote no bars' flake is dead, and it was
never key-dependent: buildHarmonyEditor deferred the wheel's opened() to

stoop/280e4ab:
The press now carries a face of its own. Anton (OFL), cut down to Latin
and №, rides inside the page as a @font-face data URL, so every headline,
marker, stencil, stamp and cover number is set the same on every machine
and in every issue file the press hands on. The PDF writer reads the same
bytes back out of the stylesheet and embeds them as a TrueType subset
(WinAnsi, with № in the euro's seat), takes its width table from the
font's own advances, and puts the first baseline where the browser does.
A headline breaks on paper where it broke on screen because both measure
the same glyphs; a stamp's lettering is sized by its box rather than the
window; the cover's rhythm on paper is views.css in points.

Also: double-clicking a marker or ransom cutting lands in its field,
Escape leaves the field with the cutting still chosen, and typographic
dashes and quotes reach the paper as themselves.

Law 9 holds the face in the built page. test/10-typeface proves the font
in the PDF is the font in the page byte for byte, that the screen's ruler
and the PDF's /Widths agree, and that the baseline formula matches the
browser. The paste-up suite now reads only content streams, since the
embedded face is binary and full of parentheses.
